title: Demand Inertia and the Hidden Impact of Pharmacy Benefit Managers
eligible_reason: Not eligible: the reduced-form 'event study' (Figure 1) regresses drug-year prices and formulary coverage on cumulative counts of two kinds of competitor events (comp_launch_event_counter, comp_loe_event_counter: number of branded competitor launches and competitor losses of exclusivity in the drug's ATC-4 class to date) with product and year FE. The regressors are multi-valued event counts with repeated events and two simultaneous treatments, not a single binary adoption; the dynamic version stacks relative-time indicators across repeated events. Table 2 is a cross-sectional class-year FE regression. The main contribution is a structural model (MATLAB). Reduced-form data are scrambled.
design_notes: Figure 1.do: reghdfe log_WAC / log_net / geruso / frac_preferred / frac_unrestricted / frac_covered on comp_launch_event_counter comp_loe_event_counter, absorb(Product_ID year) cluster(Product_ID); log_units with absorb(Product_ID age); dynamic version with _g_3.._gg3 counters for both event types. Table 2.do: areg frac_preferred/frac_covered log_net [log_WAC] [i.firmid], absorb(class_year). Inputs: combined_pricing_regression_dataset_annual_scrambled.dta, combined_formulary_regression_dataset_annual_scrambled.dta (SSR Health / MMIT, scrambled). Structural inputs are public-derived.
main_or_robustness: robustness (reduced-form motivation for the structural model)
data_provenance: scrambled (README: 'scrambled data with the correct data structure' for all reduced-form results; MarketScan demand data not shipped)
software_notes: Stata for reduced form and MEPS; MATLAB for structural estimation.
screener_notes: Flag ft_sun_and_abraham likely refers to a citation in the text about event-study estimation with multiple events. Screened from package only.
